questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Although the school lunch passed the legal standards, __________ or not it is healthy is debatable.
questions.solution:
Answer: whether

‘Whether’ means 'the expression of a doubt between two alternatives'. In the given context, the choice is between school lunch being healthy or not. Hence, ‘whether’ is an appropriate fit.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

Omkar generously donated money to the orphanage.

options.text: Money was generously donated to the orphanage by Omkar.
Money is generously donated to the orphanage by Omkar.
Donating of the money generously was done by Omkar.
Donating of the money generously is done by Omkar.

questions.solution:
Answer: Money was generously donated to the orphanage by Omkar.

Sentence 2 converts the past tense to present and makes the change incorrect. Sentences 3 and 4 change the subject from ‘money’ to ‘donating’ and make the change incorrect. Only Sentence 1 preserves the tense and structure of the sentence, making it the correct choice.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

My grandfather said to the visitor, "Who are you? Where do you come from?"

options.text: My grandfather enquired the visitor who are you, where do you come from.
My grandfather enquires the visitor who he was and where he came from.
My grandfather enquired of the visitor who he was and where he came from.
My grandfather enquires the visitor who are you, where do you come from.

questions.solution:
Answer: My grandfather enquired of the visitor who he was and where he came from.

Sentence 1 incorrectly converts the present tense (are), while Sentence 2 keeps the reporting verb in the present tense and Sentence 4 combines the above two mistakes. Only Sentence 3 changes the tense properly and is the correct answer.

questions.question: yogis in pretzel-like contortions at __________ end of the spectrum
questions.solution:
Answer: one

Spectrum is used to classify something with two extreme points. Therefore, a spectrum has two ends. Hence, ‘one’ is an appropriate choice to fill in this blank as it denotes one extreme point on the spectrum.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

His shoes (to cover) with mud.
questions.solution:
Answer: were covered

Since the subject is shoes, the verb must be in the plural form, which leaves us with Options 2 and 3. Option 3 the past continuous tense, which does not fit in with the sentence. Therefore, Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The tropical storm (be) a hurricane
questions.solution:
Answer: will become

The sentence talks about how a tropical storm will change into a hurricane in the future, requiring the use of the future tense. Hence, Option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

As Benjamin ran (1)/ next the street, he wondered (2)/ what he should buy. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Answer: 2

The word ‘next’ makes the sentence grammatically incorrect as it does not specify the relativity. It should be replaced by ‘along’, which shows that Benjamin was running on the street.

The correct sentence is: As Benjamin ran along the street, he wondered what he should buy.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Lambency
questions.solution:
The word opposite in meaning to "Lambency" is **"Dullness"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lambency:** A soft, radiant light or glow. (Hindi: चमक, प्रकाश)
 
• **Dullness:** Lacking brightness, intensity, or liveliness; lacking interest or excitement. (Hindi: उदासी, मंदता)
 
• Explanation: Lambency refers to a soft, radiant light or glow. It suggests a gentle and pleasant illumination. On the other hand, dullness refers to the lack of brightness, intensity, or liveliness. It implies a lack of interest, excitement, or brilliance. Therefore, these two words are opposite in meaning as one signifies brightness and radiance while the other suggests a lack thereof.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Dullness**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's provide the meanings of the remaining options:
 
 
• **Effulgence:** Radiant splendor or brilliance; a shining or glowing brightness. (Hindi: उज्ज्वलता, प्रकाशितता)
 
• **Gusto:** Enthusiastic and vigorous enjoyment or appreciation. (Hindi: उत्साह, मनोहारिता)
 
• **Phosphorescence: **The emission of light without burning or visible heat; a luminous appearance. (Hindi: उज्ज्वलन, प्रकाशन)

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Seventeen students were needed for a ___________ in order to discuss the topics during the Student Council meeting.
questions.solution:
Answer: quorum

‘Quorum’ means ‘the minimum number of members of an assembly or society that must be present at any of its meetings to make the proceedings of that meeting valid’.

The meanings of the other given options are:

Decorum: behaviour in keeping with good taste.

Quota: a limited or fixed number or amount of things.

Quote: repeat or copy

Therefore, 'quorum' is the correct word to fill in the blank as per the context of the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Emphasis
questions.solution:
Answer: Significance

'Emphasis' means 'special importance given to something'. 'Significance' means 'the quality of being important'.

Hence, the words have similar meanings. 'Ignorance' means 'lack of knowledge', 'triviality' means 'lack of seriousness' and 'lethargy' means 'lack of energy'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Once and for all

options.text: Now and for the last time; finally
To be successful in the first attempt
To do a charitable act for the benefit of everybody

questions.solution:
Answer: Now and for the last time; finally

The phrase ‘once and for all’ means finally or permanently. Hence, option 1 is the correct answer. An example sentence is: ‘The police shut down the smuggling ring once and for all’.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
Answer: Annoyance

The correct spelling is ‘Annoyance’, meaning 'the feeling or state of being irritated'.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The considerations which

X-are set forth in our

Y-lead us to refer ideas to the brain

Z-physiologies and psychologies
questions.solution:
Answer: YXZ

It is clear on reading the sentences that X must be followed by Z since ‘set forth’ refers to the ‘physiologies and psychologies’. This makes XZ a combination, which is seen only in Option 1. Hence, YXZ is the correct choice.

questions.question: yoga has often borne the brunt of being __________ in extremes
questions.solution:
Answer: seen

Being is generally followed by the third form of the verb, which is ‘seen’ in this case. Hence, ‘seen’ is the appropriate choice for the blank.

questions.question: erstwhile-overweight beach posers ____________ the other.
questions.solution:
Answer: at

To comply with the comparison to a spectrum, the beach posers are placed ‘at’ the other end of the spectrum. Hence, ‘at’ is the correct choice here.

questions.question: may mean lengthening muscles to gain _______________, while for someone
questions.solution:
Answer: flexibility

Flexibility is the quality of bending easily without breaking. A runner needs flexibility to run faster and longer, which he can gain from yoga. Hence, flexibility is the appropriate choice to fill in this blank.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

It was a somewhat

X-carried it off as

Y- trying ordeal, but we

Z-best as we could
questions.solution:
Answer: YXZ

The passage must begin with sentence Y as it is the only sentence that fits the flow of the opening sentence. This combination is seen only in Option 1, making YXZ the right choice.

questions.question: it could be a way of __________core strength.
questions.solution:
Answer: enhancing

The word ‘enhancing’ is the present participle of ‘enhance’ and fits with the tense of the sentence and the ‘of’ word. Hence, enhancing is the correct choice here.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

It had a bright blue (1)/ cover, which he was (2)/ careful not do soil. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Posterior
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Dorsal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Posterior"** means situated at the back or rear. (पीछे का)

 
 
• **Example:** The posterior part of the building was damaged in the storm.
 
 
 
• **"Dorsal"** refers to the back or upper side of an organism. (पीठ का)
 
 
• **Example:** The dorsal fin of a dolphin helps it to maintain stability while swimming.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to **'Posterior'** is **'Dorsal'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Dorsal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Anterior** (सामने का): Situated before or at the front.

 
 
• **Example:** The anterior part of the car was damaged in the accident.
 
 
 
• **Antecedent** (पूर्ववर्ती): A thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.
 
 
• **Example:** The antecedent events led to the company's success.
 
 
 
• **Former** (पूर्व): Having previously filled a particular role or been a particular thing.
 
 
• **Example:** The former president of the club attended the meeting.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Turgid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Humble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Turgid"** means swollen and distended or congested; in a broader sense, it can also refer to language or style that is tediously pompous or bombastic. (सूजा हुआ)

 
 
• **Example: **The turgid river threatened to overflow its banks after the heavy rains.
 
 

 
• **"Humble" **refers to having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's own importance; it can also mean not proud or arrogant. (विनम्र)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite his immense wealth, he remained humble, treating everyone with respect and kindness.
 
 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Turgid'** is **'Humble'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Humble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bloated **(सूजन): Swollen with fluid or gas.
 
 
• **Example:** After eating too much salty food, she felt bloated.
 
 

 
• **Puffy **(फूला हुआ): Swollen or distended, especially from fluid or air.
 
 
• **Example: **Her eyes were puffy from crying all night.
 
 

 
• **Tumescent** (सूजा हुआ): Swollen or becoming swollen, especially as a response to sexual arousal or in a medical context.
 
 
• **Example:** The tumescent tissue indicated an inflammatory response.
